notes.note: The [Picture-in-Picture][1] player now has a playback speed setting, with options ranging from 0.25x to 2.0x speed. The setting appears only when the player window is medium-sized or larger. [1]: https://support.mozilla.org/kb/about-picture-picture-firefox

Mini Window moves a tab or a selected part of a page into an always-on-top window while browsing. We’d appreciate feedback on [Mozilla Connect][1] as we develop and improve this early version of the feature. [1]: https://connect.mozilla.org/t5/discussions/mini-window-beta-is-going-live-in-firefox-160-and-we-want-your/m-p/144137#M59048
History entries can now be dragged from the sidebar to the tab strip to open them in new tabs.
The address bar context menu now shows "Paste and Search" instead of "Paste and Go" when the copied text is a search term rather than a web address.
Pages saved as PDF now make mathematical content (MathML) accessible to assistive technology such as screen readers.
Websites that repeatedly ask to handle email (mailto:) and other links can now be blocked with a new “Never allow” button, and blocked sites can be managed in Settings.
Firefox now plays Matroska (MKV) files with FLAC, MP3, or PCM audio.
WebGL content on macOS is now rendered using Apple's Metal graphics API, which can improve performance on some sites.

In [Smart Window][1], Organize Tabs is now available in French. Firefox can suggest groups of related open tabs and name each group in the language of the tabs.


  [1]: https://www.firefox.com/smart-window

The [`SpeechRecognition`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/SpeechRecognition) interface of the [Web Speech API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Web_Speech_API) is now supported, providing on-device, real-time speech-to-text in 40 languages.
Firefox now supports the legacy `::-webkit-input-placeholder` pseudo-element as an alias of `::placeholder`, to improve compatibility with websites that use it to style placeholder text.

For Firefox Enterprise updates and fixes, see the [Firefox Enterprise Release Notes][1]. For policy changes, see the [Firefox admin docs changelog][2].


  [1]: https://www.firefox.com/firefox/enterprise/160.0/releasenotes/
  [2]: https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/release-notes/version/firefox-160/
Fixed the first character typed into the address bar or search bar sometimes being lost when typing quickly right after clicking into it.
Increased the contrast between the domain name and the rest of the address in the address bar, making it easier to see which website is open.
Fixed Firefox freezing for several seconds when signing in to intranet sites that use NTLM or Kerberos (Negotiate) authentication.
Fixed double-tapping or long-pressing a word to select it, and tapping to place the cursor, not working near the cursor in text fields.
Fixed links opened in the background from other apps on macOS, such as RSS readers, bringing Firefox to the foreground.
Fixed downloaded files on macOS sometimes opening in the wrong application instead of the default one set in Finder.
Fixed simultaneous downloads on macOS never finishing when Firefox is set to ask where to save files. Only the first file showed a save dialog.
Restored meaningful filenames and the usual save workflow for PDFs opened in Preview from the macOS print dialog.

Various [security fixes][1].


  [1]: https://www.mozilla.org/security/advisories/

With the release of Firefox 160, we are pleased to welcome the developers who contributed their first code change to Firefox in this release, 22 of whom were brand new volunteers! system_requirements:
## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later 

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*


- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (glibc 2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (libstdc++ 6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio
title: Firefox 160.0 Release
